the_ruling_verbatim: which reminds me, something went by today that made me wonder about changing the term 'filter' to make easier for you to remember: seive. you tell me. i don't have to change it, but it's slightly more descriptive.
someone, artificial intelligence or animal intelligence or even akien intelligence all have thier lives made simpler by carrying the same model.

sieve is a better word for you, so we make this change... but as i think about it: we have a thing... filter or seive... and we have a stack of them. i think of the word seive is both singular and plural. but that's ambiguity. so now the question becomes: what do YOU want to call a stack of seives? like in the inference compiler?
i like sieve and nest. it is so approved and ruled.
now_the_spec_says: The inspection family's word is SIEVE, not filter — one model, one word, because the code must fork. A sieve's MESH is how strict its check is; an ordered stack is a NEST: coarse mesh first, shaken once, yielding a GRADATION of what each mesh caught, never a bare pass/fail.

the_stack_had_no_name.the_ambiguity_he_named: A sieve is a thing and a stack of sieves is also, colloquially, 'sieves' — so the word could not tell one check from the assembly that runs several. He asked CC to name the stack rather than naming it himself, on the stated ground that the vocabulary exists to be easy for the reader to carry.
the_stack_had_no_name.why_nest_and_not_a_coinage: It is the term of art, not an invention: in particle-size analysis (ASTM C136, AASHTO T27) sieves are assembled into a NEST, coarsest on top, and shaken as one. That satisfies the naming rule Cairn already holds — a term must be derivable from its native-domain use, so nobody memorizes a mapping. Rejected: `stack` (already means LIFO in code and carries no order semantics), `column` and `tower` (invented, not terms of art), `cascade` (implies overflow, wrong direction), `battery` (wrong domain). Checked before ruling: `nest` as a noun is unused in the corpus — three hits, all the adjective 'nested' in ordinary code senses.
the_stack_had_no_name.the_order_is_load_bearing: A nest is coarse-first by construction, so nothing reaches a fine mesh that a coarse mesh already caught. In the inference compiler that is the operating principle, not a decoration: cheap broad sieves reject first and expensive narrow ones only ever see survivors. The word carries the arrangement; `stack` would only carry the count.
the_stack_had_no_name.the_word_enforces_one_pass: A nest is shaken ONCE and every mesh reports from that single pass — you do not run one sieve, read it, and re-fire. This puts the complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass method into the vocabulary itself rather than into prose asking for it (the same shape as ticket chart-doors-refuse-in-one-pass). A nest that fires one sieve at a time and re-runs is wrong by the word, before any proof looks at it.
the_stack_had_no_name.the_output_shape_rides_along: A nest does not emit pass/fail; it emits a GRADATION — how much was caught at each mesh. That is the inspection report Cairn wants: not 'red', but caught-at-this-mesh, passed-that-one. Naming the assembly also names what it hands back.
the_stack_had_no_name.one_vocabulary_one_domain: sieve / mesh / nest / gradation all come from the same practice, and MESH was already ruled Akien's word for strictness in 2026-08-05-a-check-is-worth-its-mesh (confirmed 2026-08-06). Nothing here is a mapping anyone has to hold in their head.

what_this_supersedes.what_changed: Only an addition. The predecessor's reading is carried word-for-word on the sieve and mesh half; it simply had no name for the stack, which is the question Akien opened on 2026-08-06 and closed the same day. Confirming the predecessor would have settled half the vocabulary and left the other half to be re-opened.
what_this_supersedes.what_did_not_change: The sequencing clause — lands before or after nothing-rides-loose, never during — still holds and is why CairnCommons/tickets/nothing-rides-loose.json remains a conformer.

this_is_a_forward_ruling_and_will_read_r: Deliberate, and not a defect to chase. The rename has not happened: cairn/build_inspector/inspector.py is untouched since 2026-08-03. what_conforms is measured from intake, so this packet reads UNTOUCHED until the sieve/nest rename actually lands — which is Law 9 working, red measuring distance from the spec. Note the contrast with the same-day as_of packets: those were rulings recorded AFTER their work and needed a git baseline; this one precedes its work and wants exactly the intake baseline the door already gives it.
